log.text: This texture is my least favorite as it is attempting to emulate light casting down on the wall beneath. Can we cut this texture up so light can actually shine through it? The "cut" would remove the light grid areas of the texture, and you'll place a lightsource behind it that casts light through, being divided by the grid just like the texture on the wall beneath.

Done, three parts. (1) The grate texture's bright grid cells are now real holes (about 2,700 texels of its two panels; the bars and the rust stay solid), so you can see up through them. (2) The platform's top slab casts no shadow, so light from above can reach the grate. (3) A pale white light hangs above the platform, slanting down through both panels onto the steep slope beneath. Its light comes through only where the holes are, so the grate's bars throw a real grid of light cells onto that slope, next to the painted one. Two notes: from straight above, the light only grazed that slope, so it comes down at an angle from your side. The real grid lands slightly offset from the painted grid, so you'll see a faint double grid on the right patch; I can line them up, or tone the painted one down, if you'd like. New room settings make this reusable: 'holes' (cut a texture's bright art into openings) and 'noCast'.
changes: rooms\MINEHEAD.json (new): holes 37-mineplab, noCast 38-mineplat, a light through the grate
